project.name: entity-resolution

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: README.md introduces the entity resolution tool: LLM-aided probabilistic resolution of entities in enterprise legal and insurance documents, with auditability and provenance. CLAUDE.md complements it with a architecture summary and the commands for the legacy CLI, the API and the frontend. Read these first to learn the vocabulary used in every later step.

tour.title: Configuration and Tooling
tour.description: config.yaml selects the remote (OpenAI) and local (Ollama) LLM models and overrides generation settings, so it governs how every pipeline run behaves. pyproject.toml, managed by uv and requiring Python 3.12+, pins the backend dependencies and supersedes the stale requirements.txt. Knowing these explains how the backend is configured before reading its code.
tour.languageLesson: pyproject.toml is the standard Python project manifest. Tools like uv read it to resolve and lock dependencies, replacing hand-maintained requirements.txt files.

tour.title: The Legacy Pipeline: run.py
tour.description: run.py is the most depended-on and widest-reaching file in the project. It implements the core LLM-based pipeline: chunking, entity and relationship extraction, and graph resolution. Both the engine and the evaluation script build on it, so understanding it explains where entity resolution actually happens.

tour.title: Ontology Templates
tour.description: engine/template.py defines Pydantic ontology templates (Person, Company, Agreement, Asset, OtherEntity). These typed schemas describe what an extracted entity looks like and give the Docling-based extraction a structured target. They provide the shared vocabulary for the engine adapter in the next step.
tour.languageLesson: Pydantic models declare typed fields as class attributes and validate data at runtime, making them a natural way to describe an extraction schema for an LLM.

tour.title: Engine API Adapter
tour.description: engine/api.py runs the Docling-graph pipeline and the full resolution flow, then writes results in a backward-compatible file structure. It bridges the ontology from Step 4 and the legacy pipeline from Step 3 into a single callable layer for the web API. debug_logger.py supports it by recording LLM prompts, responses and hallucinated entities for auditability.

tour.title: FastAPI Backend
tour.description: api/main.py exposes endpoints to upload documents and start entity-resolution runs and to read their results. It delegates the heavy work to the engine API from Step 5, keeping HTTP concerns separate from resolution logic. This is the contract the frontend consumes.

tour.title: Frontend Bootstrap and Routing
tour.description: index.html loads main.jsx, which mounts App.jsx into the DOM, and App.jsx maps URLs to page components. This is the entry point of the React client that talks to the API from Step 6. Vite and the frontend package manifest drive the dev and build tooling.

tour.title: Upload and Run Workflow
tour.description: Uploads.jsx lists documents, UploadNew.jsx posts a new document and starts a run, and RunCreating.jsx polls the run status before redirecting. Together they form the user journey that triggers the backend pipeline. Runs.jsx lists all runs for later review.

tour.title: Inspecting Results and Provenance
tour.description: RunDetail.jsx shows resolved entities for a run, Document.jsx displays the source document, GraphView.jsx renders the entity graph, and Relationships.jsx lists relationships. These pages deliver the auditability promise by letting users trace results back to the source text.

tour.title: UI Primitives and Styling
tour.description: Card, Table, Button, Badge and Input are shadcn-style primitives built with Tailwind classes and reused by the pages. index.css holds the theme variables and Tailwind layers, configured by tailwind.config.js and components.json. This shared layer keeps the pages visually consistent.

tour.title: Evaluating Against Ground Truth
tour.description: test.py compares a run's extracted entities and relationships to ground truth files. It relies on the pipeline from Step 3, closing the loop by measuring the quality of the resolution results.
